meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
You have an incomplete rib fracture.
Just as I assumed.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have to tell me.
Did you chop the carrots?
Why do you not wear it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты опять намекаешь, что я толстый?
examples.trans: Are you hinting again that I am fat?

examples.text: Нет, я просто говорю, что был стройный.
examples.trans: No, I am just saying that you were slim.
What is the matter, Lyova? Easy.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'receiver, handset' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вика, а ты чего трубку не берёшь?
examples.trans: Vika, why are you not picking up the phone?
Don't hang up!
He isn't answering the phone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have an incomplete rib fracture.
No. Stop it!
And why do I not know?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'do you take/get', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: You have an incomplete rib fracture.
Did nobody take the truffles?
We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just as I assumed.
And why do I not know?
I do not owe you anything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Я изменился, я сейчас это докажу.
examples.trans: I have changed, I will prove it right now.
Am I so fat right now?
I will explain everything right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Заодно объясню, почему всё так вышло.
examples.trans: At the same time I will explain why it all happened this way.
Forgive me, I mixed everything up.

examples.text: Спасибо, Соломон Иванович. Теперь всё можно!
examples.trans: Thank you, Solomon Ivanovich. Now everything is allowed!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I'll explain everything later.
Explain, please.
I will explain everything to you right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'yesterday', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yesterday I walk into the locker room.
Yesterday I was at home.
Yesterday was Friday.

заходить.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'зайти'.

examples.trans: Please come in.
Come in, Fedya. Sit down on the chair.

examples.text: Шеф, инспектор уже заходит в зал!
examples.trans: Chef, the inspector is already entering the hall!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
You have an incomplete rib fracture.
You said it was a crack.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'девалка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'locker room' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Yesterday I walk into the locker room.
The waiters change clothes in the locker room.

examples.text: Хорошо, пойдём скорее в нашу раздевалку.
examples.trans: Alright, let's go quickly into our locker room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
Just as I assumed.
You said it was a crack.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: Louis, did you not see them?

examples.text: Ты что, не видел, что я здесь стою?
examples.trans: Did you not see that I am standing here?

examples.text: Этого вообще никто не видел. Правда, Макс?
examples.trans: Nobody saw a thing at all. Right, Max?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just as I assumed.
Be glad. How was the injury sustained?
Keep living just like before.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Whether anyone watches things here or not.

examples.text: И вижу, как кто-то роется в наших вещах.
examples.trans: And I see someone rummaging through our things.
Finally someone is for the people!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'rummages, digs through'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и рыться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and rummages on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют рыться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to rummages.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Елена Павловна нашла мой старый костюм.
examples.trans: Elena Pavlovna found my old suit.

examples.text: И вижу, как кто-то роется в наших вещах.
examples.trans: And I see someone rummaging through our things.
I love our town.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И вижу, как кто-то роется в наших вещах.
examples.trans: And I see someone rummaging through our things.
I've brought you your things.
Where are my things?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Probably a thief. I ran after him!
Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'thief' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And I will speak only the truth.
I speak only the truth!

examples.text: Нет, я просто говорю, что был стройный.
examples.trans: No, I am just saying that you were slim.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'him', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, that is what it is.
She is my niece.
And it will be a bit too big on me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слышь, ты когда врал, мне больше нравился!
examples.trans: Listen, I liked you better when you lied!

examples.text: Вы никогда на диету не садились, шеф.
examples.trans: You never went on a diet before, chef.

examples.text: Когда я перебегал дорогу, меня сбил Иосиф Пригожин.
examples.trans: When I was running across the road, Iosif Prigozhin hit me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'бегать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'ran across'.

examples.text: Когда я перебегал дорогу, меня сбил Иосиф Пригожин.
examples.trans: When I was running across the road, Iosif Prigozhin hit me.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и перебегать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and ran across on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рога'). Common feminine noun meaning 'road, way' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здорово! Я тогда быстро переодеться сбегаю.
examples.trans: Great! Then I will quickly run to change clothes.

examples.text: Когда я перебегал дорогу, меня сбил Иосиф Пригожин.
examples.trans: When I was running across the road, Iosif Prigozhin hit me.
This is a bad road.

meanings.en: to knock down, to hit, to strike
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'knocked down, hit', paired with 'сбивать'.

examples.trans: Iosif Prigozhin hit me!

examples.text: Когда я перебегал дорогу, меня сбил Иосиф Пригожин.
examples.trans: When I was running across the road, Iosif Prigozhin hit me.
The driver knocked down a road sign.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.trans: Lavrov, you are losing your touch.
You're wasting your time.
He always loses his keys.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'qualification, touch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Lavrov, you are losing your touch.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть квалификация.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always qualification.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('some kind of').

examples.trans: What nonsense.
Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'качественный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('low-quality, shoddy').

examples.trans: Some kind of low-quality lying.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень некачественный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very low-quality choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'lying, fib' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Some kind of low-quality lying.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть враньё.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always lying.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And I will speak only the truth.
I speak only the truth!
In a week you will recover.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'said', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: You said it was a crack.
You have to tell me.

examples.text: Вот что ты ей хочешь сказать?
examples.trans: Now what do you want to say to her?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Я тебе правду сказал! Что мне сделать?
examples.trans: I told you the truth! What should I do?
We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Sit down right here and do not strain yourself.
Well there, something like that.

examples.text: Вот что ты ей хочешь сказать?
examples.trans: Now what do you want to say to her?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если можно, пусть это останется между нами.
examples.trans: If possible, let this stay between us.
Let it stay between us!

examples.text: А вот пусть Иосиф Пригожин приедет и расскажет.
examples.trans: Well let Iosif Prigozhin come here and tell it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will arrive', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?
Pasha has arrived.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.trans: Tell me what happened.
I'll tell Mum everything.
Tell that to Stalin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
Well, that is what it is.
Only a wardrobe fell.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.trans: I wanted to look like you.
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will believe', paired with 'верить'.

examples.text: То есть Пригожину ты поверишь, а мне нет?
examples.trans: So you will believe Prigozhin, and not me?

examples.text: Вика, подожди! Не отпущу, пока не поверишь.
examples.trans: Vika, wait! I will not let you go until you believe me.
Forgive me for not believing you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No. Stop it!

examples.text: Нет, я просто говорю, что был стройный.
examples.trans: No, I am just saying that you were slim.
Whether anyone watches things here or not.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, what a handsome suit!
Listen, how slim you used to be!
Vika, listen, I really have changed.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cognac' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Kostyan, did you break the cognac?

examples.text: Там был коньяк, и он дешёвый был.
examples.trans: There was cognac there, and it was cheap.

examples.text: Слушай, ты не мог сказать, что Пригожин коньяк разбил?
examples.trans: Listen, could you not say that Prigozhin broke the cognac?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke', paired with 'разбивать'.

examples.trans: Kostyan, did you break the cognac?
Did you break something?

examples.text: Я? Нет, я ничего не разбивал.
examples.trans: Me? No, I did not break anything.
